title: Vibe Coded Kaiju Game
author: HallucinatedGames
selftext: I built a Vibe Coded Kaiju game. I used Claude Code with Agent Teams (Main Building Team), Meshy AI (AI Generated 3D Asset Models), Google Lyra (Music), and ChatGPT (Some Images). I'd love to hear folks funny or interesting ideas to improve the game. I have GitHub repo where I share how I built it - the code, prompts, etc - [corycowgill/Kaiju](https://github.com/corycowgill/Kaiju)

comments.author: MightyBig-Dev
comments.body: Lmaooooo this is awesome and very well done my dude. Great job!

comments.author: Intelligent_Roll_644
comments.body: This looks fantastic! As a kid I love the game Rampage and this reminds me of it. Perhaps slow down the Kaijus movement a bit, have it turn slowly (like how you control Halos warthog) to make it more rampaging 😋

replies.author: HallucinatedGames
replies.body: Thank you! Good feedback. I’m using meshy.ai which generates the 3d model, textures, and rigs the model fir animation, and they have like 200 prerecorded animations. It’s moving like a person not a monster lol cause that’s what they have in their genAI animation library. I’ll think on it!

comments.author: AimDev
comments.body: Really cool. How long did it take you?

replies.author: HallucinatedGames
replies.body: Good question. At this point, human time (me) has been maybe 20 hours over the past two or three weeks. The agents probably 80 hours churning. I give the agents big tasks and sometimes small ones. The biggest time was me having to use Meshy.AI. That’s probably 14 of the 20 hours. They have an API I considered giving to the agent team instead of me doing the prompts but I was worried they would burn through money (its usage based) without oversight.

replies.author: AimDev
replies.body: Thanks for the detailed break down. I'm a game dev but I haven't experimented with Claude code or Meshy yet. I mainly use Unreal and the integrated AI tools aren't production ready yet. I could make what I see in the video in Unreal in about 5-10 hours. As the tools develope more, I'm definitely going to augment my workflow. For now, the best AI has to offer me is high level design rubber ducking in a chat session though.

replies.author: HallucinatedGames
replies.body: I have no game dev experience, but I’m a lifelong gamer. This is very much vibe building, no formal agentic harness, no formal context engineering or specs to do a professional grade build. Similar to what I’m experiencing professionally in software, I think more of the professional gaming  platforms will come out with agentic harnesses in their suites (or skills / MCP servers) for the professionals.

replies.author: AimDev
replies.body: I keep wondering how much of what I do now will be 10x easier when the right tools for context handling are native to Unreal. There are a few plugins that are great for learning but ultimately useless, and in the worst case, detrimental for actual production work. Just having the ability to feed context to Claude from within the editor would go a long way, but everyone seems focused on the power of vibe coding. I'm not against it, but I just haven't seen it work in a meaningful way in editors yet. Very much looking forward to using them though
